definitions.explanation: A casual sentence-ending particle expressing possibility or uncertainty. Short form of かもしれない.

examples.japanese: ⟦それ→それ：00994_sore⟧、⟦{正|ただ}しい→正しい：00893_tadashii⟧かも。
⟦ちょっと→ちょっと：00595_chotto⟧⟦{難|むずか}しい→難しい：00517_muzukashii⟧かも。⟦{一人|ひとり}→一人：00630_hitori⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{無理|むり}→無理：01558_muri⟧かもしれない。
examples.english: It might be a bit difficult. It might be impossible on my own.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
かも is the casual truncation of かもしれない (might, perhaps). It attaches directly to the plain form of verbs, adjectives, and nouns:
- Verb: ⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧かも (I might go)
- い-adjective: ⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧かも (it might be expensive)
- な-adjective/noun: ⟦{好|す}き→好き：02355_suki⟧かも / ⟦{学生|がくせい}→学生：00610_gakusei⟧かも

USAGE:
Very common in casual spoken Japanese. Using the full かもしれない sounds more careful or formal. かも alone has a softer, hedging tone and is often used when the speaker wants to avoid being too direct.
